arxiv-2204-07198.creator: Sylvester Aboagye, Alain R. Ndjiongue, Telex M. N. Ngatched, Octavia A. Dobre, and H. Vincent Poor
arxiv-2204-07198.description: Abstract Recent intensive and extensive development of the fifth-generation (5G) of cellular networks has led to their deployment throughout much of the world. As part of this implementation, one of the challenges that must be addressed is the skip-zone problem, which occurs when objects such as trees, people, animals, and vehicles obstruct the transmission of signals.

arxiv-2501-16950.description: Abstract We present the development and experimental implementation of diffractive optical elements designed to generate optical vortices in the deep ultraviolet range (260–266 nm). These elements, fabricated using advanced lithographic and etching techniques, facilitate the efficient transformation of Gaussian beams into twisted modes carrying orbital angular momentum.

arxiv-2508-21603.title: On the boundary Carrollian conformal algebra
arxiv-2508-21603.creator: Lucas Buzaglo, Xiao He, Tuan Anh Pham, Haijun Tan, Girish S Vishwa, Kaiming Zhao
arxiv-2508-21603.description: Abstract . We initiate the mathematical study of the boundary Carrollian conformal algebra (BCCA), an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra recently discovered in the context of Carrollian physics. The BCCA is an intriguing object from both physical and mathematical perspectives, since it is a filtered but not graded Lie algebra.

pmc-10851146.title: Elucidating common pathogenic transcriptional networks in infective endocarditis and sepsis: integrated insights from biomarker discovery and single-cell RNA sequencing

pmc-10851146.description: BackgroundInfective Endocarditis (IE) and Sepsis are two closely related infectious diseases, yet their shared pathogenic mechanisms at the transcriptional level remain unclear. This research gap poses a barrier to the development of refined therapeutic strategies and drug innovation.MethodsThis study employed a collaborative approach using both microarray data and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data to identify biomarkers for IE and Sepsis.
